definitions.title: Multivariable Chain Rule
definitions.statement: If z = f(x, y) is differentiable and x = g(t), y = h(t) are differentiable functions of t, then z is a differentiable function of t, and its total derivative equals the sum of the partial rates along each path variable.
definitions.explanation: Can be visualized as a tree diagram with branches from z to intermediate variables x and y, and then to independent variable t.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Sums contributions to change from all intermediate coordinate paths.

definitions.title: Chain Rule for Two Independent Variables
definitions.latex: \frac{\partial z}{\partial u} = \frac{\partial z}{\partial x}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u} + \frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}, \quad \frac{\partial z}{\partial v} = \frac{\partial z}{\partial x}\frac{\partial x}{\partial v} + \frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}
definitions.statement: When intermediate variables x = g(u, v) and y = h(u, v) depend on multiple parameters u and v, partial derivatives with respect to each independent variable follow separate branch summations.
conditions: All functions possess continuous first partials
definitions.explanation: Essential for converting differential equations between Cartesian, polar, cylindrical, and spherical coordinates.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Extends coordinate transformation calculus to partial differential equations.
